review.basis: Complete source allocation retains independent authority, historical preservation, nonblocking context, finite administrative installation and consumer release-audit exclusions. Canonical independent knowledge profiles, conditional G2+ readiness and complete source-derived mandatory instructions in view, additional context and owned activation are reviewed together with local generated-output comparison; producer fixtures do not prove live delivery or comprehension.
review.preservation: Complete current clauses retain independent authority, real project outcomes, authentic history and non-authorizing examples; the delimited native activation pointer preserves entry and ownership boundaries.
review.formalization: Structured boundaries refer to complete semantic clauses. They do not decide semantic judgments or manufacture facts. Formal bootstrap guards are necessary checks, not sufficient authorization.
review.coreRationale: Precedence, authority, proportionality, language, consumer exclusions, state separation and evidence invariants apply across routes. Entry/context/workspace add current identity and availability; conditional business modules remain on demand.
review.dependencyRationale: Dependencies are conservative prerequisites from reviewed meaning. Effectful branches add action/security/execution facets even when a request initially seems informational. Context assembly never grants authority.
limitations: Semantic review performed by the producing AI; no independent human/second-model approval claimed.
Evidence records identify the evaluated subject, scope and actual outcomes.

enforcement.semantic_review: Capability-based instructions preserve authority, timing, scopes, finite administrative completion and independent native permissions. Installation records use neutral control identifiers. Material operation arguments remain exact under documented scalar/path normalization. Separate presentation metadata requires an explicit documented operation profile and a permitted completion/delegation/recovery contact point. The framework computes the full original native input identity independently; no native field name is implicitly omitted. Changed material arguments, stale dependencies, replay and invented progress remain non-authorizing. Stable installation invocation, current component identities, scoped native consent and eligibility-before-read bookkeeping remain binding. Producer neutrality exceptions are exact and contextual and do not certify semantics or installed-provider behavior. Context-loss events invalidate both loaded module records and delivered procedure records. Index reload does not reinstate discarded module records. Module identities bind the bytes parsed for delivery. Bounded module pages bind the ordered selection and current content, and session delivery records require complete module sequences at a current session revision. Coordination diagnostics expose field paths and the applicable public schema. Classification templates and recent action receipts carry scoped references without granting effects. Independent admission, resource, authority and replay checks remain binding. Completion repair requires an observed scoped obligation and is deduplicated by the action and relevant state independently of presentation and module bookkeeping. Active ticket work requires current authoritative presence, scope-bound publication and attributed checkpoints. Conditional allocation and semantic classification remain with authorized backend and runtime responsibilities. Completion diagnostics correlate registration, applicability and admission without granting authority. Repetition is scoped independently of repair permission. A documented native repeat response retains blocking. Scoped rendering recovery preserves bounded corrective context.
enforcement.source_normalization: CRLF to LF for producer templates and generated JavaScript; preserve maintained file encoding and layout.

Abstract.reason: Describes the source-bound shared instruction view and independent runtime outcomes.

Vision.reason: Names reusable methods and verification guidance as organizational knowledge independent of work-item lifetime.

Goal.reason: Connects reduced reconstruction with reusable knowledge without claiming measured savings.

Introduction.reason: Describes neutral upgrade guidance and shared-view verification.

core.use: Always applies: precedence, authority, proportional G0-G4 governance, language, evidence and continuity invariants for every request and effect.
core.conditions: Applies to every route; stronger source-qualified gates win over convenience, memory or tool defaults.
core.preconditions: Current workspace and adopted identity; explicit user authority; governance level classified before material effects.
core.postconditions: No unknown promoted to success; claims backed by actual evidence; user informed in the resolved language.

workspace.use: Before reading or writing private state, or when the project or working directory changes: establish project identity, private layout and runtime isolation.
workspace.conditions: Private state belongs to exactly one project/workspace; runtime-owned and common scopes stay separate.
workspace.preconditions: Discovered project root, protected private root and resolved owned/common locators.
workspace.postconditions: No cross-project reuse; ambiguous ownership preserved and dependent use blocked.

shared-context.use: Sharing hints, messages, leases, coordination entries or runtime instructions with other runtimes of the project: use attributable, conflict-safe records.
shared-context.conditions: Shared records are scoped data, never authority; shared instructions project canonical policies; concurrent writers must not lose updates or reuse IDs.
shared-context.preconditions: Same-project binding, provenance, freshness and an exclusive-create or compare-and-swap write primitive.
shared-context.postconditions: Conflicts preserved, material facts promoted to canonical state, expired entries not treated as current.

activation.use: Opening a bound workspace or repairing owned activation: resolve binding and entry, then read the verified shared instruction view.
activation.conditions: Activation refers to the verified shared view; peer-owned adapters are never rewritten or proof of adoption.
activation.preconditions: Persistent workspace binding and current verified entry/bootstrap reference.
activation.postconditions: Owned adapter resolves the current binding; stale references self-healed or reported as blockers.

capabilities.use: Installing, reusing or changing native enforcement and its adapters: follow the frozen administrative installation and adapter rules.
capabilities.conditions: One host-native adapter per installation and host; administrative completion, not functionality certification.
capabilities.preconditions: Host environment, selected native shell, validated configuration plan and required native consent.
capabilities.postconditions: Mechanisms installed or reused with direct acknowledgments; real failures halt dependent effects.

knowledge.use: Before dependent organizational G2+ work: assess knowledge, reuse or acquire canonical profiles, verify publication and load applicable coverage.
knowledge.conditions: Changed scope, knowledge needs or escalation invalidates affected coverage; authorized preparation and independent work continue.
knowledge.preconditions: Current effective scope, canonical profile references, source quality, actual capability and authorized conditional publication.
knowledge.postconditions: Coverage and used versions reconstructible; gaps block dependent work only; profile lifecycle survives ticket closure.

cost.use: Choosing a tool, service, dependency or any action with a monetary or quota cost: prefer adequate free/local options and justify paid ones.
cost.conditions: Free-first applies unless security, reliability or authority would be compromised.
cost.preconditions: Known alternatives with their setup and recurring costs.
cost.postconditions: Selection rationale recorded; no paid dependency without justification and authority.

repository.use: Discovering, creating, binding or writing a repository, or committing and pushing: resolve provider-neutral scoped access before effects.
repository.conditions: Inaccessible is never absent; no duplicate creation after 403, ambiguous 404 or timeout.
repository.preconditions: Four-state discovery result, selected credential and verified read/write capability.
repository.postconditions: Remote state read back; ref targeting and publication verified, not inferred from command success.

security.use: Credentials, identities, signing, access rights, or commits and publications carrying an identity: use project-authorized identity and separate proofs.
security.conditions: No ambient or foreign credentials; authentication, write and signature acceptance verified separately.
security.preconditions: Project-scoped credential reference, effective actor and attribution identity.
security.postconditions: No raw secrets persisted; identity and signature of the actual object verified.

model.use: Representing organizational entities, sources of record or dependencies: keep one canonical English representation with external references.
model.conditions: No fabricated entities; external systems of record are referenced, not duplicated.
model.preconditions: Current canonical model revision and authoritative external references.
model.postconditions: Model changes consistent with the dependency graph and recorded in canonical form.

operations.use: Reading or writing the canonical operations repository, foundational intake or publication of organizational records.
operations.conditions: operations is distinct from project source, the OOP checkout and .priv; four-state discovery applies.
operations.preconditions: Resolved operations identity, verified runtime read/write access and expected revision.
operations.postconditions: Canonical writes published atomically, read back remotely and attributed correctly.

inventory.use: Listing, retrieving or updating the inventory of relevant repositories and resources of the organization.
inventory.conditions: Inventory reflects discovered relevant repositories only; unrelated scanning is avoided.
inventory.preconditions: Current operations access and repository references.
inventory.postconditions: Inventory entries current, attributable and non-duplicated.

intake.use: A request whose meaning, scope or level is uncertain: discover effective scope and ask proportionate clarification before effects.
intake.conditions: Clarify only what blocks responsible planning; never stall G0/G1 work with ceremony.
intake.preconditions: Received request and known context; open questions identified.
intake.postconditions: Effective scope defined, or clarification pending with dependent work blocked.

impact.use: Work whose consequences may spread to other components, domains or capabilities: determine effective scope and propagate proportionately.
impact.conditions: Effective scope can exceed the literal request; new capabilities only when genuinely necessary.
impact.preconditions: Classified request, organizational model and dependency information.
impact.postconditions: All material consequences identified and dispositioned before completion.

tickets.use: Work needing durable continuity or managed governance (typically G2+): open or attach a ticket or equivalent item before effects; report each transition.
tickets.conditions: G0 may stay ephemeral and G1 may use existing issue, PR or version control evidence; G2-G4 need managed facts.
tickets.preconditions: Classified governance level, effective scope and expected prior ticket state/revision.
tickets.postconditions: Each creation and transition durably published, read back and reported to the user; completion gate satisfied.

changes.use: A change to source, configuration or content that must be reviewed and verified: define the change set, apply it, verify it against effective scope.
changes.conditions: Desired, approved, applied and verified states stay distinct; scope expansions are re-evaluated.
changes.preconditions: Governing work item, reviewable change set and authorization for its scope.
changes.postconditions: Applied change verified against success criteria; outstanding effects tracked.

coordination.use: Planning or executing work affecting several organizational functions: coordinate only materially involved roles, without inferred authority.
coordination.conditions: Involve necessary roles only; coordination never grants authority to any participant.
coordination.preconditions: Identified affected domains and their accountable owners.
coordination.postconditions: Cross-domain dependencies resolved or tracked with responsible owners.

execution.use: Performing any material effect, retry or verification: track intended, attempted, observed, applied and verified effects separately.
execution.conditions: A timeout or exit code is not proof of effect; non-idempotent retries need inspection first.
execution.preconditions: Authorized action proposal with expected prior state and verification criteria.
execution.postconditions: Actual effects observed and verified; partial effects recorded for informed recovery.

migration.use: Transforming shared organizational data or changing read/write compatibility: plan ownership, concurrency and verification of the migration.
migration.conditions: Organizational migration is separate from runtime adoption and performed once under exclusive authority.
migration.preconditions: Canonical revision, actual state interpretation and reader/writer compatibility.
migration.postconditions: Migration result verified and canonically recorded without blind replay.

migration-distribution.use: Adopting a newer OOP distribution carrying technical migrations: apply the three-scope descriptors in order, without assuming ancestry.
migration-distribution.conditions: Common, runtime and operations scopes reconcile independently; unknown profiles block dependent work.
migration-distribution.preconditions: Supported profile match from authenticated scope-bound state observations.
migration-distribution.postconditions: Required descriptors applied and verified; prior adoption retained on failure.

adoption.use: An OOP update is available or due: check freshness, compatibility and authorization, then adopt independently per runtime.
adoption.conditions: Discovery or download never adopts rules automatically; peers keep independent checkpoints.
adoption.preconditions: Observed remote identity, current adopted commit and authorization to adopt.
adoption.postconditions: Owned checkpoint updated atomically after verification; knowledge realigned.

continuity.use: Context or compute budget is running low, or work may be interrupted: keep the reserve and prepare destination-independent continuation.
continuity.conditions: Use the 15% reserve only with reliable comparable measurements; never invent percentages.
continuity.preconditions: Reliable budget signal and current work state.
continuity.postconditions: Continuation material prepared before the reserve is exhausted.

handoff.use: Transferring work to another runtime, model, person or session: prepare a portable baseline and evidence each handoff phase separately.
handoff.conditions: Preparation is not delivery and delivery is not resumption; no credentials in the package.
handoff.preconditions: Current work state, access continuity plan and governing work items.
handoff.postconditions: Each phase evidenced; destination validation pending until observed.

destination.use: Starting work received through a handoff: perform independent intake, filter resources and keep the source/target firewall.
destination.conditions: The destination never inherits source adoption, authority or unchecked claims.
destination.preconditions: Own identity, adoption and access verified at the destination.
destination.postconditions: First verified action performed before claiming resumption.

secret-transfer.use: A secret must reach another runtime or person: reuse existing access first and transfer separately only when necessary and authorized.
secret-transfer.conditions: Secrets never travel inside handoff packages, logs or coordination records.
secret-transfer.preconditions: Authorized need, recipient identity and a separate secure channel.
secret-transfer.postconditions: Transfer confirmed without exposing values; references updated.

recovery.use: Resuming after interruption, crash or context loss: reconstruct verified context and actual effects before continuing.
recovery.conditions: Summaries are navigation only; never replay non-idempotent work blindly.
recovery.preconditions: Owned checkpoint, actual effect observations and current freshness.
recovery.postconditions: Context rehydrated and remaining action re-authorized before dependent effects.

decisions.use: A significant decision is made or must be recalled: record it durably with rationale and related work.
decisions.conditions: Record only significant decisions; avoid duplicate records of the same fact.
decisions.preconditions: Decision content, authority and related work items.
decisions.postconditions: Decision record published canonically and linked to affected work.

human.use: Progress depends on an action or decision only a human can provide: state the exact dependency and resume automatically once verified.
human.conditions: Only true human-only dependencies justify waiting; independent safe work continues.
human.preconditions: Proved human-only dependency and persisted scoped checkpoint.
human.postconditions: Prerequisite verified and work resumed without repeated requests.

physical.use: Work with physical-world responsibilities, constraints or safety: plan observable completion and accountable owners.
physical.conditions: Physical effects need observable verification; digital records alone do not prove them.
physical.preconditions: Responsible owners, constraints and observation method.
physical.postconditions: Completion observed, or explicitly pending with accountable follow-up.

ci.use: Checking consistency of a change set across dependencies before delivery: run proportionate checks and semantic compilation.
ci.conditions: Checks are risk-proportionate and free-first; passing structure is not semantic proof.
ci.preconditions: Defined change set and the applicable checks.
ci.postconditions: Check results recorded; failures block dependent delivery.

delivery.use: Deploying or applying an approved change to a controlled environment or external system: apply gates, compensation and drift handling.
delivery.conditions: Remote transport alone is not G3; material external effects need G3 controls.
delivery.preconditions: Approved change set, risk gates and compensation plan.
delivery.postconditions: Applied state verified externally; drift detected and handled.

history.use: Reconstructing what happened and why, or recording a material event: keep causal, non-fabricated history and reuse evidence.
history.conditions: Never fabricate past times or transitions; reuse evidence by reference.
history.preconditions: Actual event evidence and causal references.
history.postconditions: History reconstructible without duplicate or invented records.

interfaces.use: Exposing organizational state to external tools or formats: project canonical English state without creating a second source of truth.
interfaces.conditions: External projections are derived views, never authoritative stores.
interfaces.preconditions: Canonical state revision and target interface contract.
interfaces.postconditions: Projection consistent with canonical state and labeled as derived.

producer.use: Maintaining, testing or publishing the OOP repository itself (maintainer only); never part of consumer routing.
producer.conditions: Producer commands and release checks are excluded from every consumer lifecycle.
producer.postconditions: Release evidence bound to finalized content; publication verified by readback.

context.use: Every interaction and governed action: load or rehydrate the closure; prepare effects and apply scoped procedures and declaration (R26).
context.conditions: Changed context invalidates affected reuse; preparation and procedural candidates require current bindings and attributed semantic review.
context.preconditions: Current route, closure identities and context integrity state.
context.postconditions: Only valid context reused; stale or missing context rehydrated before dependent effects.

entry.use: Start of each conversation and each user message: pass the entry and interaction gates, resolve language and load minimum context.
entry.conditions: Applies to new, resumed and recovered chats alike; conversation age grants no exemption.
entry.preconditions: Workspace binding, adopted identity and resolved presentation language.
entry.postconditions: Request classified and applicable closure loaded before substantive work.

bootstrap.use: Explicit OOP installation or interrupted setup: run the listed BOOT steps with stable identities, scoped attestation and user communication.
bootstrap.conditions: Full installation only on explicit intent; ordinary requests use progressive bootstrap.
bootstrap.preconditions: Scoped install intent, project identity and protected private root.
bootstrap.postconditions: Each step verified or explicitly pending; identity registration published and read back.

delegation.use: Delegating work to a sub-agent or delegate runtime: apply the same contract, owned controls and validated completion.
delegation.conditions: Delegates never widen authority; their completion is validated before acceptance.
delegation.preconditions: Delegate scope, adoption and controls verified.
delegation.postconditions: Delegated results validated against the same postconditions.

migration.review_evidence: Reviewed initial source distribution and independently owned state contracts; no release predecessor or migration effects are asserted.

current.state_schema: Initial OOP contract: independent installation ownership, canonical reusable knowledge profiles, conditional G2+ readiness, complete source-derived mandatory delivery and scoped local generated-context verification.
current.read_compatibility: Verify per-domain actual state under existing canonical policy.
current.write_compatibility: Current knowledge/profile semantics, canonical conditional publication, independent runtime capability and adoption, and actual source-bound mandatory context are required before dependent work or writes. No historical backfill or peer adoption is inferred.
current.existing_state_policy: Preserve safely interpretable history and adequate canonical knowledge; reconcile current coverage, mandatory generated views and owned activation before dependent work. Never fabricate historical profile use, replay shared effects or rewrite peer-owned checkpoints.

common.rationale: The initial distribution has no predecessor; common installation and actual-state reconciliation remain independently required under current authority.

runtime.rationale: The initial distribution has no predecessor; runtime installation and actual-state reconciliation remain independently required under current authority.

operations.rationale: The initial distribution has no predecessor; operations installation and actual-state reconciliation remain independently required under current authority.

enforcement_transition.before: A new installation starts without an active integration. An existing installation may expose a different contract.
enforcement_transition.after: The root-first controller directs the runtime to the shared workspace view, verifies both mandatory texts at its head and routes technical adoption independently from organizational knowledge work.
enforcement_transition.rationale: An initial installation requires its own compatible declarative adapter. Reuse an observed current complete-context forwarding adapter when its documented limits and actual administrative prerequisites remain valid; reconcile only owned incompatible state. No predecessor release or peer adoption is asserted.
